messages:
Diane S: FYI — Acme Fintech (Mei) asked for committed capacity guidance for their Q3 POC. They want to support up to ~1000 req/s peak for a chat + embeddings flow. They also want reserved GPUs (commit) + autoscale burst and clear pricing. Can we draft sizing + cost + any security notes?
Raj P: Quick clarifying q's: average tokens per request? target p99 latency? are embeddings served on same model infra or separate? budget ballpark?
Mei Chen: avg generation ~250 tokens, some flows hit 1024 but rare. embeddings requests are smaller (avg 64 tokens) and ~30% of traffic. Target 99.9% business-hours availability. Budget: want a committed monthly cap, prefer predictable monthly spend vs huge overages.
Carlos M: Heads-up — 1000 req/s @ 250 tokens is non-trivial. We should present two options: conservative reserved baseline + autoscale/burst plan, or commit to larger pool. Also recommend caching/prefix KV for chat to reduce work.
Carlos M: Raw calc I usually use (pseudocode):
```
qps = 1000
avg_tokens = 250
tokens_per_gpu_sec = 4000   # empirical for quantized 7B-ish on A100 (varies by model/seq)
gpus_needed = ceil((qps * avg_tokens) / tokens_per_gpu_sec)
# => ceil(250000 / 4000) = 63 GPUs (if we did full generation on 7B without cache/optimization)
```
Carlos M: That number is intentionally conservative and shows why we need other levers: shorter models, quantization, KV/prefix cache, batching, or routing some traffic to smaller models.
Lauren K: Pricing note — for reserved commits we price by GPU-hour commit + discounted overage. Example SKU (placeholder): $3.00 / GPU-hour committed; overage $4.50 / GPU-hour. Monthly cost example (baseline 6 GPUs): 6 * 730 * $3.00 = $13,140/month. If they reserve 12 GPUs baseline = ~$26k/mo. We'll provide exact quote after we finalize GPU type and hours.
Raj P: Can we propose a pragmatic POC commit? Suggest baseline for commit: support steady 200 qps of full-chat quality (low-latency) and autoscale policy to handle bursts up to 1000 qps by either spinning up extra GPUs or routing lower-priority requests to a cheaper model. That keeps commit costs reasonable and meets their peak needs.
Diane S: +1. Frame as: commit for predictable 200 qps (business-hours primary), autoscale burst to 12 GPUs for spikes, and a fallback policy that routes to a fast 3B variant when queueing would otherwise exceed SLO.
Mei Chen: That fallback sounds OK. Will they see degraded answers on fallback? We need guidance for our product team.
Carlos M: Yes, there is a quality tradeoff. We should do A/B on a small prompt set. Also recommend enabling prefix caching for conversation history — that can cut GPU time significantly for multi-turn chat.
Carlos M: Proposed concrete config:
- Baseline reserved: 6 x A100 (or equivalent) pinned to their tenant (predictable throughput for 200 qps).
- Autoscale burst: allow scale to 12 GPUs for up to 30 minutes when sustained > 250 qps, cooldown 5m.
- Routing policy: if queue latency > 150ms, automatically route <critical traffic to 3B model variant.
- Cache: enable prefix/KV caching for this app; expect ~25-40% token work reduction depending on reuse.
Lauren K: Cost example with that config (placeholder numbers):
- Commit for 6 GPUs: 6 * 730 * $3.00 = $13,140/mo
- If they hit bursts and consume average extra 6 GPUs for 50 hrs/mo at overage $4.50/hr: 6 * 50 * $4.50 = $1,350 extra
Total sample month = ~$14.5k (very rough, depends on model & exact GPU SKU).
Diane S: I'll send this as a proposed plan to Acme: commit-level baseline for predictability + autoscale/burst + fallback. Mei, can you confirm internal buy-in for the fallback quality tradeoff and whether 200 qps baseline fits their production goals?
Mei Chen: I'll confirm w/ product. Also, on security: they asked about KMS for customer keys, VPC peering, and SOC2. Any blockers?
Carlos M: We support customer-managed keys (KMS), VPC private endpoints for Private deployments, and SOC2 compliance. For Reserved (Dedicated) we can offer tenant isolation and audit logs. We should route their security questionnaire to security ops for a quick pre-filled pack.
Diane S: Action items: @Lauren K prepare cost matrix for 6/8/12 GPU commits with A100 vs A10G SKUs; @Carlos M write short runnable sizing note + recommended autoscale policy; I'll follow up with Mei on fallback acceptance and collect their security questionnaire PDF. I'll aim to send to Mei by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Redwood Deploy Bot: autoscale-policy-template v1 uploaded to /shared/sales-pocs/autoscale-templates (link: https://redwood.internal/sales/autoscale-templates) :robot_face:
Lauren K: I'll drop the pricing matrix and a sample legal-friendly sentence for commits into that folder.
Mei Chen: Thanks all — this helps. We want the proposal by EOD tomorrow so we can sync with internal procurement.
Diane S: Great. If we need to tighten numbers before the proposal, we can run a short perf run next week on the customer's representative prompt set. That will give us tokens_per_gpu_sec for their actual workload.
Raj P: I'll coordinate the perf run scheduling with Mei.
Diane S: Closing note — we'll avoid overpromising 1000 qps on the high-quality model w/o a perf run. We'll offer the two-path plan (predictable commit + burst + fallback) in the proposal.
